newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-China's absence continue to haunt.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-China's absence continue to haunt.

text.p: Singapore's gas oil market continued to be haunted by China's absence from the market which is placing a bearish pall on the market, traders said on Tuesday.
"The Chinese are not really back yet," one trader said. "Chinese demand are still thin and even enquiries for barges in Hong Kong are not that much."

They said even the scheduled shutdown of the 200,000-barrel-per-day crude unit at Indonesia's Cilacap refinery in October for up to three months would only have a neutral effect on the middle distillate market.
This is because additional supplies would emerge from South Korea as more refineries would return from maintenance shutdowns there, they said.
Three sellers--a US major, European major and a Mediterranean trader--offered early September barrels at between $22.60 and $23.20 per barrel. But buyers were uninterested.

Traders said the market was confused on Monday when a Singapore trader who offered at $22.80, withdrew it after buying a 200,000-barrel lot at a 40-cent-per-barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes, free-on-board (fob) basis.
The swaps gas oil market was also quiet in rangebound trading reflecting the lack of demand from the region.
Physical jet fuel was again well supplied with four offers--from two majors, a Chinese trader and a Swiss trader--offering at higher levels of between $23.30-$24.00 per barrel.
Traders said such high offers were unlikely to attract any buying interest.

They said recent news of companies fixing jet fuel cargoes for shipment to the U.S. West Coast are not due to the opening of the arbitrage window but due to traders taking positions by keeping cargoes in U.S. storage in anticipation of improved prices.
They said the impact of such moves are also not expected to be felt strongly in the market.
